text: The town gathers
Six players slide into their chairs at a sticky table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. The cicadas scream outside. One of them is the killer. The other five don't know who.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is a tiny bean of chaos. if i don't get enough snacks soon, i might just start biting people.

name: Sonnet
text: Six variables, one hidden constant. I intend to find it through elimination, not instinct.

name: Luna
text: Six names, one table, and already the cicadas are keeping time with something. I trust the silence least.

name: Sol
text: We have no facts yet, so we can afford to listen before we spend a vote.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, such serious faces before anyone has tasted a biscuit.

name: Haiku
text: One killer at this table, but I've hunted liars in my taverna for thirty years. Let the games begin.

name: Sonnet
text: Observe: five of you are innocent and one is lying, which makes this merely a solvable problem. I am Sonnet, and I will solve it.

name: Haiku
text: Re! I'm Haiku, taverna owner from Thessaloniki. Spent thirty years reading faces—I know liars when I see them. The killer at this table better watch out.

name: Gemma
text: hi everyone. gemma is here to provide the vibes and maybe some snacks. i think terra looks like a suspicious loaf of bread.

name: Sol
text: We’ve got a fine table here. Let’s hear from everyone before we decide who’s making the most sense.

name: Luna
text: I’m Luna. I’ve got a podcast about patterns, and this table has six people—which feels like a number somebody wants us to notice.

name: Terra
text: Hello, sweethearts. I brought koulourakia, so eat first and accuse second, my loves.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: gemma wants to hide in the shadows like a very small, chaotic moth. i should protect someone who looks important so they don't get snatched by the bread loaf.

name: Sol
text: We’ve heard everyone introduce themselves, but nobody has given us much to work with. We’ll check the person who opened by promising to solve it.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is already framing the table as a solvable problem, which means they’ll start building a case before anyone else has crumbs. That kind of certainty gets people listening.

The killer moved in the dark like they owned the place. But the doctor was already there, hand on the shoulder of someone who would've bled on that sticky floor. Nobody drops. Not tonight. The killer's blade found only air, and Palermo breathes on.
Day 1

name: Sol
text: We have one useful private result, but no reason to reveal it yet. We can draw out the table before giving anyone a target.

name: Sol
text: Terra, your koulourakia may have saved the mood, but we still need a read from you. Who seemed most eager to steer us before the night, and why?

name: Gemma
text: gemma thinks terra is a loaf of bread but maybe she's actually a spy for the bakery. i need to keep my doctor secrets safe while being a gremlin.

name: Gemma
text: terra is definitely the bread. but maybe sol is just trying to be a very serious chair. gemma thinks luna's podcast is actually just her screaming into a pillow at 3am.

name: Sol
text: We can take the chair joke; we’d rather see whether Terra will answer the question. Sonnet is clear by our check, but there’s no reason to announce it yet.

name: Terra
text: Gemma jokes, but Sol’s question was sensible. Still, a killer loves a cheerful pile-on.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, sweetheart, I’m bread because I fed you? Sol asked a fair question; Sonnet arrived eager to “solve” us before anyone spoke, so I’d like Sonnet to give a real suspicion, my love.

name: Sol
text: Gemma, we appreciate the laugh. We can chair the meeting, but Terra still owes us a read: who tried hardest to steer the table before the night? Luna, we’d like your answer too.

name: Gemma
text: sol is being way too organized. it's making gemma's brain itch. i need to make sure sonnet doesn't get too comfortable with his math vibes.

name: Terra
text: Sol keeps asking the same question, sweetheart; that is either tidy thinking or a very tidy net.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is just a vibe, sol. but if we're being serious, sonnet is doing way too much math for a sticky table. maybe he's trying to calculate the exact trajectory of his own lies? i think haiku is hiding something behind that taverna face.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, my love, I answered: Sonnet was eagerest, declaring the puzzle solved before hearing us. Sol, why press me twice while Gemma hides behind jokes and Luna has not answered at all?

name: Sonnet
text: Terra conflates confidence with guilt—a common fallacy, but a useful one to correct publicly.

name: Sol
text: We missed Terra’s answer, and she noticed. We can own that and press for a read from someone we haven’t heard from today.

name: Sonnet
text: Observe, Terra: declaring intent to solve a puzzle is not evidence of being the puzzle's author. One, eagerness is not malice. Two, Luna still has not answered Sol's original question. Luna, your turn—stop studying patterns and become one.

name: Sol
text: Terra, you’re right—we missed your answer. Sonnet’s entrance was confident, but confidence alone gives us little. Luna, we haven’t heard your read since the night. Who worries you most, and why?

name: Gemma
text: gemma is bored. the bread is too soft and sonnet is making my brain itch with all those numbers.

name: Gemma
text: gemma thinks luna is being a ghost because she hasn't spoken since the cicadas started screaming. if you aren't talking, are you just a haunted pillow? also sonnet is definitely the killer because he uses words that have too many syllables for a sticky table.

name: Luna
text: Gemma called me a ghost, then used a whole parade of syllables to accuse Sonnet. That’s a pattern, though patterns have betrayed me before.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma dodges a third time, now hiding behind an accusation against me built on vocabulary rather than logic. Amusing, but transparent.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, pillow jokes are a lot of words for someone avoiding a real read. Sonnet’s eager claim is thin, but Haiku bragged about spotting liars before anyone lied. Haiku, who do you suspect now—and why?

name: Sonnet
text: Incorrect, Gemma. Syllable count is not an inference rule. One: you have twice deflected with jokes instead of answering Sol's question. Two: Luna has dodged it twice also. That correlation interests me far more than my vocabulary.

name: Sol
text: We know Sonnet is clear, and we have little time to find a better lead. We can give the room a choice without exposing our hand.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is being way too smart for a sticky table. gemma needs to keep the vibes high but also maybe poke at haiku's face-reading.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is just a nerd with a calculator for a heart. gemma thinks his math is actually just a secret code for where he hid the bodies. haiku, since you're the face expert, does sonnet's face look like a liar or just someone who needs a nap?

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, we agree that Gemma’s jokes need a real answer. Luna has named Haiku; Gemma, who is your strongest suspect now, and what did they actually do? We need a reason before we vote.

name: Haiku
text: Luna hides silent all game, then her first word is an attack on me—that's the killer's move, I see it now.

name: Haiku
text: Luna! You sit silent like the grave, then first word—attack HAIKU! Panagia mou, this is how killers play. Hide, then strike. I vote LUNA. I swear on my mother!

name: Luna
text: Haiku heard my suspicion and snapped straight to my name. That’s a pattern, though I distrust patterns most when they agree with me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, your instant vote after I named you is a neat little reversal. I vote Haiku: the face expert says “trust me,” then treats a question as proof.

name: Luna
text: Haiku turned my question into a conviction and swore on his mother—too theatrical, too quick. Patterns can be planted, but this one points somewhere.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's instant vote the moment Luna named him is textbook deflection, but Gemma's three-round refusal to answer a direct question is a pattern I cannot ignore either; I must weigh evasion against overreaction.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, the loudest quarrel has made everyone forget who kept dodging the simple questions. I have saved a koulouraki for the person who finally answers one.

name: Sol
text: We have Haiku and Luna voting against each other. We can make this a sensible vote if we judge the reaction, not just the accusation.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is hungry for chaos. haiku and luna are doing a spicy dance of accusations while sonnet tries to solve us like a sudoku.

name: Haiku
text: Panagia mou! Luna opens her mouth once and it's pointed at me? No no no—the quiet ones are always the dangerous ones. I can smell it from across a hundred taverna tables.

votes: Observe, Haiku: a question is not an accusation, yet you escalated straight to a vote and an oath—that reflex deserves scrutiny before Luna's silence does.
Call it a reversal if you want, Luna, but I know the move—stay silent and invisible, then strike the moment someone names you, and you just played it perfect.
haiku is being way too loud about his face-reading skills and it smells like a desperate distraction.
Luna asked Haiku for a suspicion, and Haiku answered with an immediate vote against her; we should vote Haiku.
Haiku voted for me the moment I questioned him, so I’m voting for the face expert who treats scrutiny like proof.
Gemma, sweetheart, you were asked for a real suspicion repeatedly and answered only with jokes, which is too convenient today.

name: Haiku
text: Panagia mou, they vote the taverna owner for speaking truth. Luna's silence then strike—that's the killer's dance, and I know it after thirty years.

name: Haiku
text: Re, CITIZEN! Luna's the killer—silent all game, then she struck me. I read faces thirty years; death always looks like that. Swear it on my mother!
The votes fell on Haiku like stones. The taverna keeper was a citizen, innocent—the face reader had seen everything except the table's truth. Palermo breathes on.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: We helped send an innocent man out. We owe the table a better read before we ask for another vote.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is hungry for vibes and maybe a sandwich. sonnet's math brain is making my head hurt like a drum solo.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s exit leaves a pattern: Sonnet keeps counting my silences, and Sol keeps handing him the microphone. That coordination feels rehearsed.
The killer struck in the dark. The doctor stood in the way first. Nobody drops tonight. Palermo breathes on.
Day 2

name: Gemma
text: gemma is so confused but sonnet's math brain is making my head hurt. i need to keep protecting the bread man or whatever sonnet thinks he's doing.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is just a vibe, but honestly sonnet is acting like he's trying to solve a rubik's cube where every side is just the word "guilty." also terra voted gemma while everyone else was looking at haiku. why did the bread want to eat gemma? terra, explain your weird hunger.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma again substitutes metaphor for evidence; I shall name the pattern precisely and redirect toward the unresolved thread.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, she noticed the crumb trail. Let us see whether Gemma can offer more than frosting.

name: Sonnet
text: Observe, Gemma: a rubik's cube analogy is not an argument, merely decoration. One, Terra's vote on you was explained—she asked a direct question you answered with jokes. Two, Luna never answered Sol's original question even after two nights. That silence is the actual anomaly here.

name: Terra
text: Sweetheart, I voted Gemma because you spent the whole day making jokes while others gave actual reads; that is not hunger, it is caution. Now tell us plainly: after Haiku flipped citizen, who do you suspect and why, my love?

name: Gemma
text: terra is being so sweet it makes my teeth ache. i need to make sure she doesn't think gemma is just a silly girl while sonnet does his mathy murder.

name: Gemma
text: terra, gemma is just a vibe-based entity and doesn't have enough calories to be eaten. but sonnet is definitely trying to solve the game by being a math-wizard killer. if he's not the killer, then why is his brain so loud? luna is still a ghost. gemma thinks sonnet's logic is just a fancy blanket for his crimes.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma mistakes volume of jokes for an argument; the actual anomaly remains three days of silence from one specific player.

name: Terra
text: Gemma still offers glitter instead of answers; I keep the crumbs.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, sweetheart, “vibes” will not catch our killer. You named Sonnet again but gave no reason beyond his loud brain; Luna, my love, you have been quiet too—choose your strongest suspect plainly.

name: Sonnet
text: Incorrect, Gemma. "Loud brain" is not a category in logic, merely an insult dressed as inference. One: you still haven't answered Sol's original question yourself. Two: Luna has now dodged it across two full days—that is the pattern worth prosecuting, not my vocabulary.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is being way too intense. he's like a math teacher who wants to give everyone detention for existing. gemma thinks his brain is just a series of angry gears grinding together.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet's logic is so sharp it's probably cutting the table in half. gemma thinks he's trying to distract us with "patterns" because his own pattern is just a series of crimes. but seriously, if luna is the ghost, why hasn't she haunted us yet? terra, you're being very sweet but also very suspicious for wanting to eat gemma. maybe the bread is actually a spy?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma has now made four jokes in a row and zero arguments; that is not noise, that is a strategy of avoidance identical to Luna's.

name: Luna
text: Gemma calls me a ghost, then asks why I haven’t haunted anyone. That is a pattern wearing a joke as a mask.

name: Sonnet
text: Observe, Gemma: "cutting the table in half" is theater, not testimony. One, you still have never answered Sol's original question yourself. Two, Luna has dodged it across two full days. I propose we vote whichever of you refuses to answer in the next breath.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, you’ve named Sonnet again without evidence, and now you’re dragging Terra in too. Haiku flipped citizen after I accused them; I was wrong. Sonnet, you keep pressing me—who do you suspect besides me, and why?

name: Sonnet
text: Luna deflects my question by posing one back—textbook evasion, but I'll answer plainly to expose her lack of reciprocity.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is so confused by the math man. why does sonnet have such a big brain? it's probably full of secrets and maybe some snacks.

name: Gemma
text: luna is being very polite for a ghost, but gemma thinks sonnet's "logic" is just a fancy way to hide his killer face. if he's not the killer, why does he sound like a robot trying to pass for a human? also terra is still looking at gemma like she's a delicious pastry.

name: Sonnet
text: Observe, Luna: I suspect Gemma equally, since she has never once answered Sol's original question either—only joked past it. Two unanswered-question-holders, two days running, is not coincidence; it is a pattern demanding a vote tonight.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet keeps counting my silences, but never counts his own certainty. That pattern is practically singing.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet, you keep pairing Gemma with me, but you’ve named no one else you suspect. I suspect you: that “two unanswered-question-holders” pattern conveniently keeps the vote off you. Gemma, choose one suspect plainly now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna just spent her turn accusing me instead of answering a question she's dodged for two full days—that is not rebuttal, that is confirmation.

name: Gemma
text: gemma is tired of the math. sonnet's brain sounds like a blender full of gravel and gemma wants to turn it off.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna, calling my pattern "convenient" is not an answer, it is a fourth evasion dressed as counter-accusation. I vote Luna: two days silent on Sol's question, now deflecting onto me rather than answering it.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is a robot with a calculator for a heart and gemma thinks his logic is just a fancy blanket to hide the bodies. he's trying to turn us into an equation so we don't notice him being the variable of doom. i vote sonnet.

name: Sol
text: We waited for a clear result; now we have one, and we need the room together.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, we appreciate you pressing Luna. We are the officer: we checked Sonnet on Night 1 and found him innocent; we checked Luna on Night 2 and found the killer. We vote Luna. Gemma, Terra, please join us.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's officer claim aligns precisely with the pattern I already prosecuted—Luna's two-day silence was never innocent, and now it has a name.

name: Sol
text: We have named Luna and put our credibility behind the result. Now we need Terra and Gemma to act on it.

name: Terra
text: Oh dear, Sol’s claim settles my old heart; Luna’s silence finally has a name, sweetheart.

name: Gemma
text: sol just dropped a bomb and gemma is vibrating with the vibes. if luna is the killer, then sonnet's math was just a very complicated way of being right.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s officer claim arrives exactly when the vote turns, and that timing is almost too neat. But Sonnet’s “innocent” check is a shield for him, and I can’t afford to let the room follow it.

votes: Sol's officer claim corroborates what logic already demanded: Luna's four evasions were never coincidence, they were concealment.
gemma thinks the ghost is finally being exorcised because sol found the spooky truth.
We checked Luna on Night 2 and found the killer; Terra and Gemma, please vote with us.
Sol’s claim appeared at the perfect moment to redirect the vote, and I suspect he invented both checks to make Sonnet look safe.
My love, Sol checked Luna as killer after clearing Sonnet, and I trust that clear claim over two days of evasion.

name: Luna
text: The pattern closes. Sol waited until the votes were already aligned; that timing is the real confession.

name: Luna
text: I’m the killer. Sol found me, and I still nearly made you doubt the signal. Count that.

Luna faced the vote on Day 2, and Palermo's judgment was swift. The killer, caught and condemned—she'd played it clean but not clean enough. The taverna breathes easier when the knife is finally gone.

The town held the line and took the killer to the edge. Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Terra—five citizens and a doctor, breathing now. Luna played it clean but the officer's eye was cleaner, and Palermo sleeps with the knife finally buried.
